Plaincast decodes the National Weather Service's Area Forecast Discussion — the real forecast, written 3 to 4 times a day by the meteorologist on shift — into plain English. The discussion is where a forecaster explains their reasoning: which models disagree, what they are watching, and how confident they are. Below is the current edition for Los Angeles, with its shorthand expanded. The full experience — an AI plain-English summary beside the annotated original — loads with JavaScript, and every one of the 68 forecast offices has its own edition.

Area Forecast Discussion · National Weather Service Los Angeles (LOX) · issued Friday, July 3 at 4:40 AM PDT.

Synopsis

Low clouds and fog will continue each night and morning with a chance of drizzle near the coasts through the weekend across the region.

Short Term

Marine layer around 1500 feet deep this morning. A wknd warming trend is expected as high pressure builds over the region with temperatures above normal in the valleys by Saturday afternoon and evening.

This is the plain-text edition, decoded without AI so it loads anywhere. Read the whole Los Angeles discussion at /o/LOX/, see what changed since the last one, or open The National Desk for where the weather is today.
